sourceLine: your Tally fleet and UL 3300 certification, and the questions retailers ask before a robot shares the aisle

cards.title: From Pilot to Chainwide in Under Three Months
cards.angle: HomeBase USA, a nine-location retailer, expanded Simbe to all locations in less than three months after a pilot, per a July 30, 2026 release. The release reports 92% fewer pricing errors and 58% fewer controllable out-of-stocks from the pilot, with no baseline or measurement period.
cards.evidence: Your release names Tally, fixed sensors and RFID and does not state how many stores the pilot covered. Your September 21, 2026 release counts 3,000+ units under contract, which is not a deployed count. No article on your site explains which data quality signals decided the pilot-to-chainwide conversion.

cards.title: Shelf Accuracy Claims Need Their Denominators
cards.angle: Simbe's May 2025 release reports 98.7% SKU-level identification accuracy and over 99.3% shelf-condition recall, with no test population or evaluation protocol on the page. The two figures measure different things, and the article asks what was counted for each.
cards.evidence: Your Simbe Vision release cites 60 billion shelf images analyzed, 18 million SKUs and 5,400 items scanned per hour, all vendor-reported. No article on your site explains how recall is measured on a shelf, what counts as a miss and which shelf conditions were hardest to detect.

cards.title: Certifying a Robot That Shares the Aisle
cards.angle: UL Solutions certified Simbe's Tally and its charging dock under UL 3300 on March 11, 2026, and calls it UL Solutions' first global certification of a public-facing robot. Testing covered fire and shock hazards and safe autonomous mobility in public environments.
cards.evidence: UL says OSHA added UL 3300 to a recognized standards list and gives no effective date. Certification does not replace a retailer's site-specific safety assessment. No article on your site explains what UL 3300 tests and what a retailer's safety team still has to assess before the robot goes into a busy aisle.
